question: m10
q: Is the Friday dip as big for suburban morning commuters as it is for the CBD?

transcript.answer:
**Yes, it's about the same. On the broadest measure the suburban Friday dip is slightly bigger than the CBD's.** Each figure below is Friday trips as a share of the Tuesday–Thursday average (1.0 means no dip).

| | Pre-COVID (6 Jan – 6 Mar 2020) | Last 12 months | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sydney CBD**, 3–7pm tap-ons (people leaving work) | 0.905 (−9.5%) | ~0.775 (−22.5%)* | −13 pts |
| **Suburban**, 7–9am tap-ons, all modes (people leaving home) | 0.933 (−6.7%) | 0.758 (−24.2%) | −17.5 pts |
| **Suburban**, 7–9am, bus only | 0.941 (−5.9%) | 0.799 (−20.1%) | −14 pts |

*My average of the monthly CBD figures for Oct 2025 – Sep 2026, which ranged from 0.744 to 0.800. September 2026 was 0.783.

**What this shows:**
- **The dips are now about the same size.** Across all transport modes, suburban morning Friday travel is about 24% below midweek, and CBD Friday evening travel is about 22–23% below. Buses alone show a slightly smaller suburban dip (about 20%).
- **The suburbs have changed more since COVID.** Before 2020 the suburban Friday dip was smaller than the CBD's (about 7% vs 9.5%). It has since grown more, by 17.5 points against 13. So working from home on Fridays isn't just a city-office habit. It shows up just as clearly in trips starting from home across the suburbs.
- The CBD gap has been steady. It has stayed at about 0.74–0.80 every month since January 2025.

**Things to keep in mind:**
- The two measures aren't strictly the same. The CBD figure counts people heading home in the afternoon (3–7pm). The suburban figure counts people leaving home in the morning (7–9am) anywhere outside the named commercial centres. That includes students and people not commuting to an office, not just workers.
- The source doesn't give exact dates for the suburban "last 12 months" window, so it may not line up exactly with my CBD average.
- It's unclear whether Sydney Metro taps are included in the CBD data. That affects how CBD volumes compare with 2020, but not the Friday-vs-midweek ratios used here.

Source: TfNSW Opal tap data, via Commute Pulse.
